caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1835 of 2009
lawyer:
Ziaul Hasan, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Respondents ----- Not represented
parties:
Chairman, Chittagong Port Authority ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Safiuddin and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J:- Instant Retition. under Article 193 of the Constitution is for granting leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 22.01.2009  passed in Civil Revision No. 227 of 2003 by the High Court Division making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 2002 by the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, restoring the Money Suit No. 11 of 1992 to its original file and number, on an application filed under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 3. The defendant filed written statement to resist the claim of the plaintiff but the suit was allowed to be decreed ex-parte on 03.06.2000 and subsequently on receipt of auction notice from Court, the said defendant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 2002 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Money Suit No. 11 of 1992 after setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 03.06.2000. 

 4. The plaintiff of Money Suit as opposite party contested the miscellaneous case by filing written objection and the learned Joint District Judge upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record allowed the petition by order dated 31.10.2002 awarding compensation of Tk.5,000/- in favour of the plaintiff. 

 fee. Accordingly the learned Subordinate Judge fixed 8th March, 1998 for peremptory hearing. On that day the defendants did not take any step in the matter and it was adjourned to 12th April, 1998 the suit was ultimately adjourned on many occasions and ultimately it was taken up for ex-parte hearing 15th March, 1999. The learned Subordinate Judge thereupon issued show cause notice upon the defendants as to why the order dated 5th august, 1997 allowing their prayer for cross-examination of the plain-tiff should not be vacated. The defendant’s did not take any step on 31st March, 1999 and 28th April, 1999 and ultimately the suit was decreed ex-parte." and (b) "Admittedly the defendants had knowledge about the pendency of the suit and the recording of the plaintiffs evidence ex-parte. Despite that fact the learned Subordinate Judge afforded the defendants to contest the suit and allowed their prayer to cross examine the plaintiffs witness but they did not deposit the commission fees on 4th September, 1997, 25th September, 1997, 19th October 1997, 13th November, 1997, 8th January, 1998, 2nd February, 1998 and thereafter they did not take any step on 8th March, 1998, 11th April, 1998 and 11th October, 1998. Even after issuance of the show cause notice on 15th March, 1998, they did not take any step in the matter. The learned Joint District Judge himself found the neglect and laches on the part of the defendants in prosecuting the matter. The learned Joint District Judge on perusal of the evidence of P.W. 1 noticed that though the defendants imputed the blame upon their Advocate Manik Mridha but said Manik Mridha remain as panel Advocate for the Chittagong Port Trust and accordingly disbelieved their plea. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit after eight years six months of the date of institution. Thereafter they filed for setting aside the exparte decree after One year eleven months eighteen days on 19th June 2002. They did not explain the delay properly. The learned Joint District Judge was not also satisfied with the explanation and even then without condoning the delay allowed the application on flimsy ground." and (c) "As observed above, the suit was instituted in January, 1992 for recovery-of huge amount of money and for years together, the defendants were afforded sufficient opportunity to contest in the suit but they failed to take any step in the matter. The learned Joint District Judge himself found that there was neglect and laches on the part of the defendants in prosecuting the matter. The reason for which the learned Joint District Judge has set aside the ex-parte decree and allowed the Misc. Case is based upon misconception of law. The Court has no power to set aside an ex-parte decree for ends of justice or for any cause other than its satisfaction that the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. The defendants have miserably failed to satisfy the Court in that regard and accordingly, the learned Joint District Judge arbitrarily set aside the ex-parte decree without being satisfied that the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause when the suit was called on for ex-parte decree. Since the trial Court itself found that there was neglect and laches of the defendants in prosecuting the matter, it ought not have exercised the inherent powers in setting aside the ex-parte decree overriding the express provisions that there must be sufficient ground for believing that the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. The learned Joint District Judge in the premises arbitrarily exercised its discretion in setting aside the ex-parte decree which is required to be interfered with." 

 7. The learned Advocate found it difficult to overcome the laches on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the case. The learned Advocate however tried to put blame on the learned Advocate of the petitioner, who con-ducted the suit in the trial Court. 

 8. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case as disclosed in the observations made by the High Court Division, quoted hereinabove, we are of the view that the default was made by the petitioner in contesting suit. The premium given by the trial Court, in restoring the suit to its file and number in-spite of the gross negligence found on the part of the petitioner hereof in con-ducting the case cannot be sustained. We find that the decision arrived at by the High Court Division is an 'accordance with law and no interference is called for.
